subject: Annual commit proposal — three-tier usage plan & carryover mechanics
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@trellishealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@trellishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Annual commit proposal — three-tier usage plan & carryover mechanics

Hi Anna / Trellis procurement team,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great to walk through your Q1 product roadmap. As promised, attached is a concise proposal that maps to the Starter / Growth / Enterprise commit bands we discussed and a short FAQ on carryover and billing smoothing. High level:

- Starter: 150M tokens/year, $0.80 per 1k tokens (10% effective discount off list)
- Growth: 600M tokens/year, $0.64 per 1k tokens (20% effective discount)
- Enterprise: 2.5B tokens/year, $0.44 per 1k tokens (30% effective discount)

Key commercial mechanics I'm proposing in the attached PDF:
- Quarterly true-up window + monthly usage reports (we push detailed token-level exports)
- 90-day grace window for initial ramp (unused tokens may be carried forward up to 20% of the next quarter cap)
- One-time onboarding credit for model tuning & prompt engineering (applied in first invoice)
- Overages billed at the next-tier rate with 30-day notice before charge (or option to purchase top-up block)

Attachments: redwood_annual_commit_proposal_v1.pdf, usage_forecast_trellis_2027.xlsx (simple forecast sheet)

If this looks sensible, we can prepare the SOW + DocuSign and target a Feb 1 billing start (or shift to 60 days after signature per your preference). Let me know any must-haves from legal/procurement — happy to incorporate.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Anna Patel <anna@trellishealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual commit proposal — three-tier usage plan & carryover mechanics

Karthik,

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with our conversations. A couple of clarifying items before procurement will greenlight:

1) Carryover cap: when you say "up to 20% of the next quarter cap", does that apply per quarter or as a cumulative annual carry? We need to understand how much runway we actually get in Q1 if adoption lags.
2) Ramp credit: what specifically is the structure of the onboarding credit (amount and how applied)? Can that be applied to cover the initial tuning work from our vendor?
3) Billing start: we prefer billing to start 60 days after signature to allow for compliance onboarding. Would Redwood accept a 60-day bill start?

Procurement is CC'd here (procurement@trellishealth.com) for legal redlines — they'll want to see sample SOW and the specific language for termination and unused token handling.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Anna
Anna Patel
Head of Product Operations | Trellis Health
anna@trellishealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Annual commit proposal — need pricing sign-off & contractual approach

Internal — looping you both in. Anna at Trellis pushed back on two operational points (carryover semantics and billing start) and procurement will want SOW + termination language.

Proposed adjustments we should consider before sending an updated PDF to Trellis:
- Offer explicit quarterly carryover: unused tokens in a quarter can be carried into the next quarter up to 20% of that next quarter's cap. Unused tokens beyond that are forfeited (clean and audit-friendly).
- If they pick Growth/Enterprise, increase carryover cap to 30% (customer wins for committing higher).
- Make onboarding credit a line-item: $15k credit applied to first invoice OR a technical services credit (they can assign to vendor invoices with prior approval).
- Accept billing start = 60 days after signature, but reduce onboarding credit by 25% if billing is delayed >60 days (to avoid indefinite credit exposure).
- Keep overage approach as "next-tier rate" for predictability; offer option to pre-purchase top-up block at Enterprise rate if needed.

Soojin — can you confirm the suggested per-1k token prices would still preserve margin at Growth / Enterprise with the extra carryover? We should also flag any SLA credit impacts if we extend grace/overage leniency.

Marissa — if these are acceptable we can send an updated document and request procurement's sample redlines. If you want, I can draft the exact clause language for carryover and onboarding credit.

Original message attached below for reference.

Regards,
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@trellishealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@trellishealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual commit proposal — three-tier usage plan & carryover mechanics

Anna / Trellis team — cc'ing Soojin (pricing) and Karthik (AM). Per our internal review, attached is an updated one-page proposal and a short SOW snippet you can drop into your procurement process. Notes on the changes: 

- Carryover: Quarterly carryover allowed up to 20% of next quarter cap for Starter; 30% for Growth/Enterprise. Carryover expires after one subsequent quarter (i.e., carryover from Q1 must be used by Q2). This keeps the accounting simple.
- Onboarding credit: $15,000 applied as a credit to first invoice; alternatively, we can issue a $15k technical services credit that Trellis assigns to their vendor with prior approval. We'll show both options in the SOW.
- Billing start: Redwood accepts billing start 60 days after signature. If start is delayed >60 days, onboarding credit is reduced by 25% (to limit open credit exposure).
- True-up & reporting: monthly usage exports and a 15-day quarterly true-up window. Overage price = next-tier per-1k rate, with option to buy a top-up block at Enterprise pricing (fixed price for that block).
- Termination: 60-day termination notice; we proposed a short clause that unused prepaid commits are non-refundable but may be transferrable to a related entity with prior consent.

Attachments: redwood_annual_commit_proposal_v1_updated.pdf, sow-template-redwood.docx, usage_forecast_trellis_2027.xlsx

Next steps: if procurement provides redlines we will route through legal and return a DocuSign packet (I will own signature routing). Otherwise, confirm which commit band Trellis prefers and we will produce a PO-ready quote.

Thanks,
